description: Corynespora leaf spot is a destructive fungal disease affecting over 500 plant species, including economically important crops such as tobacco, tomato, cucumber, soybean, cotton, and rubber tree. Infection begins on lower or middle leaves, forming dark green water-soaked spots that turn brown and expand into large lesions. The pathogen can exist as a necrotroph, saprophyte, or endophyte, and thrives under high humidity and slightly acidic conditions.
symptoms: Small dark green water-soaked spots on leaves
Lesions expand and merge forming large patches
Disease often begins on lower or middle leaves

biological_control.mode_of_action: Produces antifungal metabolites and inhibits fungal growth
Produces lipopeptides that damage fungal cell membranes
Mycoparasitism and competition with plant pathogens
Produces antifungal enzymes and secondary metabolites

fungicides.mode_of_action: Inhibits fungal growth on leaf surface

management_notes: Rotate fungicides with different modes of action to prevent resistance
